text:
In terms of laser industry dynamics: 

- $LITE: "Take or pay. There's a very strong commitment from the customer side, and in some cases, there's a prepay element as well". Hyperscalers were explicitly funding their capacity expansion as well

- $COHR: Upfront payments in almost every LTA, according to its CEO. 

Both Lumentum and Coherent are the gold standard in terms of financing + demand signals. 

- For Chinese laser suppliers:

Optical module makers are actively financing their supply chains (even for lower range pluggables), as seen with Cambridge. 

In terms of US supply chains: 

- $AAOI CFO gave a note: "Customer financing is more likely for emerging technologies such as CPO and NPO than conventional 800G and 1.6T transceivers."

- $AAOI got a CPO + laser contract worth $700m for 2028-2029. But resulted in more ATMs instead of funding expansion with prepayments... 

I think people can agree AOI as a business at $3.7B MC is very operationally compelling:

- since they signed a $1B-$1.5B LTA with one hyperscaler
-  $2.2B LTA all in a single quarter.

But with management repeatedly creates expectations that later disclosures contrast with, which I agree is strange. 

Lot of current financing (as seen with Neoclouds) are done with prepayments given tightening. Or if a supplier is important enough (as seen with $SPCX), they'll help refinance the company. 

So I'm really not sure what's happening with $AAOI, maybe it's overstated competitive positioning or something else.

ticker_notes.NVDA: 代理AI需求強勁，CPU收入預期翻倍

zh_summary: 空頭說2027或2028年沒有AI需求。錯誤。看數據。記憶體：高盛預測DRAM在2026年短缺4.1%、2027年5.1%、2028年1.2%。2027年缺口是15年多來最寬。供應商：三星2027年HBM已售罄。SK海力士看到需求至2030年高於供應。美光沒有平衡的視線。NVDA表示代理AI對CPU的需求遠超供應，並看到CPU收入翻倍以上。GPU：三年前的H100每小時租金3.07美元，一年上漲54%。資本開支：2027年雲端支出再增60%，約1.5萬億美元。AI需求強勁。忽略末日論者。
text:
The bears say there is no AI demand in 2027 or 2028. False. Look at the data.

Memory: Goldman has DRAM short 4.1 per cent in 2026, 5.1 per cent in 2027 and 1.2 per cent in 2028. The 2027 gap is the widest in 15+ years. Demand beats supply every year.

Suppliers: Samsung’s 2027 HBM is sold out. SK hynix sees demand above supply through 2030. Micron has “no line of sight” to balance. New fabs arrive in 2028 and later.

Wafers: HBM rises to nearly 30 per cent of DRAM wafer input in 2027 and takes 3 to 4x the wafers per bit. 

Conventional DRAM gets squeezed.
CPUs: NVDA says agentic AI demand for CPUs is “far outstripping supply” and sees CPU revenue more than doubling.

GPUs: a three-year-old H100 rents for $ 3.07 an hour, up 54 per cent in a year. CoreWeave has 10x more demand than capacity through 2027, and 2028 is already several times capacity.

Capex: cloud spending is up another 60 per cent in 2027, to about $ 1.5 trillion.

If demand were fading, old chips would get cheaper. They are getting dearer.

AI demand is strong. Ignore the doomers.

text:
The memory upcycle in two charts:

DRAM:
• Contract prices started climbing in 3Q25 and were up ~45% QoQ by 4Q25
• 1Q26 was the peak: blended ASP roughly doubled in one quarter, with PC DDR5 up ~110%
• 2Q26 added another ~60%, led by server DDR4 at ~70%

NAND:
• Later and a bit smaller: ~+30% in 4Q25, ~+57% in 1Q26, ~+75% in 2Q26
• Enterprise SSD led both quarters at ~+80%

What's forecast next:
• 3Q26: DRAM ~+15%, NAND ~+20%
• 4Q26: both around +10%
• 2027: DRAM flattens to low single digits, while NAND turns negative from 2Q27 and is falling 10–15% QoQ by 4Q27

Prices are still rising, but the rate of change peaked in 1H26. And the forecasts say NAND rolls over well before DRAM does.

DOES A $VIX SPIKE MEAN BUY? THE ACADEMIC EVIDENCE, THE REBUTTALS, AND A CONCLUSION

THE CLAIM

The folk version says buy when the fear gauge screams. The academic version is narrower and more interesting: expected equity returns step up, nonlinearly, after implied volatility reaches extreme levels, and the step-up is large enough to measure years of data at a time. Across 29 historical episodes in which the VIX exceeded 30, a strategy of cutting equity exposure above 30 and buying back when volatility subsided underperformed simply holding through the episodes by 10.9% a year. Subsequent S&P 500 returns rose with the level of the VIX. Their conclusion for investors with a high appetite for risk: when the VIX is high, invest, because on average you will be compensated.

text:
🚨 This is one of the craziest things I’ve seen all year.

A newly public Google patent filing describes a TV channel that could generate shows for an audience of one. 

It could even cast you as the lead, with a character who looks like you and speaks in your voice. 

Google calls the concept “My Channel.” Open it and you’d see a lineup of titles and descriptions, much like any streaming app. 

The difference is where those titles come from. Google’s system would use your viewing history, language, location and age group to write prompts for AI to create videos specifically for you. 

Say you watch a lot of crime thrillers and comedies. 

Your channel could offer a crime comedy with you playing the detective. In one version of the design, the system would build your character from your photos and use a synthetic version of your voice to deliver the lines. 

The detail that caught my attention as a $GOOGL investor is that advertising is already in the design. 

The filing describes a system that could stitch targeted ads into the video before playback. Think about what that would mean for two people turning on their TVs at the same time. 

They could each get a different show, with a different lead character and a different advertiser. 

Things are about to get crazy.
